data.narrative:
Humans& is an AI & Software company at an undisclosed stage with five founders including Eric Zelikman and Georges Harik. The valuation universe comprises one public comparable (Palantir, ticker PLTR) and eight private peers, including Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition. However, the peer set lacks sufficient homogeneity for traditional comparable analysis.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this valuation. The AI & Software sector contains twelve same-sector peers, but rigorous filtering—by stage, adjacency, and valuation tier—yielded fewer than three datapoints in any meaningful bucket. Applying an all-sector median would introduce excessive noise and obscure material differences in revenue stage, business model, and risk profile across the broader AI universe. Standard venture methodologies therefore cannot be reliably deployed here without additional data on Humans&'s stage, revenue run-rate, or capital structure.

Absent triangulation across multiple quantitative approaches, a defensible valuation range cannot be supported by the available information. Key uncertainties blocking analysis include Humans&'s current stage of development, total capital raised to date, and revenue metrics relative to the private peer set. Progression on any of these dimensions—particularly stage clarity and comparative financials—would enable application of revenue multiples or stage-adjusted peer analysis. Current data is insufficient for a point estimate or range.
